input: Workers who come into contact with pesticide during handling must receive prompt medical treatment if signs of poisoning appear.
Operators must wear appropriate respiratory protection when the pesticide may produce hazardous vapors during use.
Personnel exposed to pesticide residues must immediately remove contaminated clothing and wash the affected skin.
Employees handling the concentrated product must follow the required personal protection measures to prevent human exposure.
The product label must state the required interval between the final pesticide application and crop harvest.
The approved label must specify the maximum number of applications permitted during a growing season.
The package label must identify the crops and application situations for which the pesticide is authorized.
The label must contain the required restrictions concerning when and where the product may be applied.
Before commercial distribution, the manufacturer must obtain authorization for the pesticide from the competent regulatory authority.
The company must renew its pesticide registration before the current authorization expires.
A new pesticide product requires regulatory approval before it can be legally marketed.
The pesticide may continue to be sold only while its regulatory registration remains valid.
Pesticide containers must be kept locked when they are not being used.
Unused pesticide must be kept in a secure location inaccessible to unauthorized persons.
Pesticides must remain in sealed containers while stored between applications.
The product must be stored separately from food and animal feed when not in use.
The applicator must observe the required waiting interval before allowing workers to enter the treated field.
During spraying, the operator must maintain the specified setback distance from a nearby residential area.
The applicator must maintain the required buffer distance from a pond while performing the treatment.
Operators must follow the specified application rate when treating the crop with the pesticide.
Pesticide use must not result in contamination of rivers, lakes, or groundwater.
The pesticide must not cause unacceptable harm to aquatic organisms in nearby water bodies.
Application of the product must be conducted in a manner that protects non-target wildlife from harmful exposure.
The use of the pesticide must not create unacceptable risks to pollinators or other beneficial insects.
The registrant must submit monitoring results to the regulatory authority at the end of the reporting period.
Any confirmed pesticide poisoning incident must be reported to the designated regulatory authority.
The company must provide the regulator with an annual report containing pesticide sales information.
Manufacturers must notify the authority when required monitoring data indicates an adverse incident.
